title: Exposed storage: public buckets and the most common mistake of the decade

videos.script: For years, the most common cloud leak needed no attack at all. {{title}} A bucket was readable by everyone. Somebody found it, and asked for the files. The bucket answered, as designed. {{decade}} Voter records, customer records, passwords. Often the bucket was a vendor's, holding somebody else's data. {{vendor}} This lesson shows the four grants that make a bucket answer a stranger. {{paths}} One is a policy. Three are access lists, and two of those live on single files, where a bucket review never looks. {{acl}} One of them even refuses the simple test, and still answers anybody with an AWS account. {{authenticated}} Then the guardrail AWS built after a decade of this: four switches, above every grant. {{bpa}} You will write a short program that asks every bucket, and every object. {{checker}} And you will fix what it finds, and prove the fix, by asking again as the stranger. {{end}}
